idiom_name: property initialisers / init blocks (vs by lazy); CoroutineStart.DEFAULT starts on creation
implementation_notes: Kotlin's eager form is the plain declaration: a val property initialiser or an init block runs when the object is constructed and top-level properties run when the file's facade class is loaded - the documentation recommends initialising properties at declaration - while by lazy is the deliberate opposite. Two Kotlin-specific facts shape the design: object and companion declarations are initialised lazily, at first access like a lazy val, so anything that must be ready at boot has to be touched during start-up or moved into a class; and coroutines are eager by creation, since CoroutineStart.DEFAULT immediately schedules the coroutine (only LAZY defers it), so readiness needs an explicit await on the warm-up Deferred rather than a check that the coroutine object exists.
pitfalls: object and companion-object members are initialised lazily at first access, so code that assumes 'declared means acquired' pays the cost - and the failure - in the middle of a request.
Coroutines are eager at creation: launching warm-up coroutines without awaiting their Deferred lets readiness be signalled while the pool is still empty.
An exception thrown from a property initialiser leaves the instance or the object's class initialisation in a failed state, which is worse than a clean boot failure.
